searchText: There has also been feedback from Vyper team to relax RETURNDATALOAD to pad with zeros instead. However RETURNDATACOPY, as it is now, throws on out-of-bounds read. This means we either have these two inconsistent in EOF, or we need to update RETURNDATACOPY's behavior in EOF, or introduce RETURNDATACOPY2 with the zero padding behavior, banning RETURNDATACOPY in EOF. One of the reasons is "appending the data section" operation happening when deploying new contract. If data section header were optional, this operation could involve inserting the header when there's no data before the operation, and that is costly. When it's mandatory we only update the size in the header. it's feedback from both vyper and solidity teams btw 🙂 fwiw, vyper would like to disable reentrancy by default, but the cost of it needs to be cheaper Right and then we right-pad them right, just like CALLDATALOAD? yes, the idea is to make it consistent with returndata, code and memory Hey all some small super-nits while reading over EOF EIP specs. https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4200: this also requires stack validation, otherwise it is possible to RJUMPx out of the container section
